error_modes.label: Chandelle - entry and completion airspeed

texts.0: SP, due to an initial pull applied late and then unloaded through the first 90 degrees of turn, did not trade airspeed for altitude at the programmed rate and did not arrive at the 180-degree point on the briefed completion speed. Airspeed at roll-out was more than 15 knots fast, the Chandelle finished with excess energy and a descending nose, and the IP took the controls to re-establish level flight.
texts.1: SP, due to a pitch attitude held below the briefed value after the 90-degree point, did not continue the airspeed bleed toward the completion speed. Airspeed at roll-out settled at the outer edge of tolerance, about 15 knots fast, and was brought back only after the IP called the deviation verbally.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly steep pitch attitude at entry, allowed the airspeed to decay faster than programmed through the second half of the Chandelle. The completion speed passed between 5 and 10 knots low, and SP recognized the trend before roll-out and relaxed back pressure to recover it without any IP input.
texts.3: SP set the entry airspeed on the briefed value and traded it smoothly against pitch and bank, arriving at the 180-degree point within 10 knots fast and 5 knots slow of the completion speed. Energy management was continuous and no catch-up correction was required.
texts.4: SP flew an airspeed profile that tracked the briefed schedule throughout the Chandelle and arrived at the completion point within a few knots of target. Pitch was adjusted in small anticipatory increments, so no correction was visible in the airspeed trend.
texts.marginal: SP kept the Chandelle completion speed inside the standards, but each repetition finished on the fast side of the band, indicating a pitch attitude set low for the bank being flown. SP should tighten the pitch and bank pairing at the 90-degree point so that the completion speed converges on the briefed value rather than on the upper tolerance.

texts_at.0: SP flew the Chandelle with the IP calling the pitch and bank pairing needed at the 90-degree point to hold the briefed airspeed schedule, since trading airspeed for altitude on a set schedule has not yet been flown without that call. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to pair pitch and bank to the schedule independently on the next Chandelle.

texts.3: SP maintained the briefed airspeed schedule at both 90-degree points and at completion, within 10 knots fast and 5 knots slow, and the energy exchange was symmetric between the two halves.

texts.marginal: SP kept the Lazy Eight airspeeds inside the standards but the second half consistently ran faster than the first, indicating that pitch was relaxed early in the descending quarter. The roll finished with the nose well below the horizon and the aircraft more than 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading, with the result that the maneuver ended as a diving turn. The IP took the controls and flew the recovery.
texts.1: SP, due to the rudder being applied late in the half roll, let the nose drop through the roll and finished 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading, at the limit of the tolerance, with the nose below the horizon, with the result that the momentary pause in level flight was replaced by a climb back to the horizon. SP applied the rudder only after the IP called the nose. The completion was made within the limitations.
texts.2: SP, due to the rudder through the half roll being a fraction less than the nose needed, let the nose sag slightly through the roll and finished about 15 degrees off the reciprocal heading, between the desired and the maximum tolerance, with the result that a small heading correction was needed at the completion. SP recognized the nose against the horizon, held it up with rudder and corrected the heading without prompting. The completion was in level flight.
texts.3: SP started the half roll as the nose reached the horizon, held the nose up with rudder through the roll and completed wings level within 10 degrees of the reciprocal heading with a momentary pause in level flight. No prompting was required.
texts.4: SP timed the half roll exactly to the nose reaching the horizon, held the nose on the horizon with rudder throughout and completed on the reciprocal heading within a degree or two with a clean pause in level flight. Nothing in the Immelman needed a correction.
texts.marginal: SP kept the Immelman inside the required standard, but the nose sagged slightly through the half roll on most Immelmans and the completion sat near the 10 degree edge of the heading band each time. The tendency is to apply the rudder late in the roll. SP is expected to apply the rudder as the roll starts.

texts_at.0: SP flew the Immelman with the IP calling the point for the half roll and the rudder through it, since timing the roll to the horizon and holding the nose up with rudder have not yet been practiced. The nose sliced down through the roll because the roll was started with the nose high and no rudder was applied. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to apply the rudder as the roll starts on the next Immelman.
texts_at.1: SP let the nose drop through the half roll and finished about 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading with the nose below the horizon, at the outer edge of the standard, due to the rudder being applied late in the roll. The rudder was applied after the IP called the nose. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to apply the rudder as the roll starts.
texts_at.2: SP let the nose sag slightly through the half roll and finished about 15 degrees off the reciprocal heading, due to the rudder being a fraction less than the nose needed. SP is expected to match the rudder to the nose through the roll.
texts_at.3: SP held the nose up with rudder through the half roll and completed within about 10 degrees of the reciprocal heading in level flight, due to the roll being started a fraction before the nose reached the horizon. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to wait for the nose to reach the horizon before the roll.

texts_above.1: SP completed the Immelman within the limitations after the nose dropped through the half roll to about 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading, at the tolerance limit, climbing back to the horizon once the rudder was applied. The rudder application followed a verbal call from the IP on the nose. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the nose sagging slightly through the half roll against the horizon, held it up with rudder and completed about 15 degrees off the reciprocal heading in level flight without prompting. Matching the rudder to the nose from the start of the roll would keep the nose on the horizon throughout. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to steady Immelman technique.
texts_above.3: SP started the half roll as the nose reached the horizon on every Immelman, held the nose up with rudder and completed within 8 degrees of the reciprocal heading with a momentary pause in level flight. The only refinement available was to wait a fraction longer for the nose to reach the horizon. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to precise Immelman technique.
texts_above.4: SP timed every half roll exactly to the nose reaching the horizon, held the nose on the horizon with rudder throughout and completed on the reciprocal heading within a degree or two with a clean pause in level flight. The technique is already sound; nothing in the Immelman needs to change. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to exemplary Immelman technique.

error_modes.label: Aileron Roll - roll rate slowing through the inverted and the nose dropping, the roll not completed on the entry heading

texts.0: SP, due to the aileron being relaxed as the aircraft passed through the inverted and the nose not being raised above the horizon before the roll, let the roll rate slow to a stop inverted with the nose falling. The roll was completed with the nose more than 20 degrees below the horizon and the aircraft more than 20 degrees off the entry heading, with the result that the maneuver ended in a dive. The IP took the controls and flew the recovery.
texts.1: SP, due to the roll rate being allowed to slow through the inverted, let the nose drop and completed the roll with the nose 20 degrees below the horizon, at the limit of the tolerance, and 20 degrees off the entry heading, at the limit, with the result that the wings were level but the aircraft was descending. SP held the aileron through the inverted only after the IP called the rate. The recovery was made within the limitations.
texts.2: SP, due to the aileron pressure being a fraction less through the inverted than the constant roll rate required, let the rate slow slightly and the nose drop, completing the roll with the nose about 15 degrees below the horizon, between the desired and the maximum tolerance, and about 15 degrees off the entry heading, between the desired and the maximum tolerance. SP recognized the rate slowing against the horizon, held the aileron and completed the roll without prompting. The recovery to level flight was made at the completion.
texts.3: SP raised the nose above the horizon before the roll, held a constant roll rate through the inverted and completed the roll with the wings parallel to the horizon within 10 degrees of the entry heading with the nose near the horizon. No prompting was required.
texts.4: SP flew the aileron roll with the nose set above the horizon, the roll rate constant through all 360 degrees and the completion with the wings parallel to the horizon on the entry heading within a degree or two. Nothing in the aileron roll needed a correction.
texts.marginal: SP kept the aileron roll inside the required standard, but the roll rate slowed slightly through the inverted on most rolls and the completion sat near the 10 degree edge of the band below the horizon each time. The tendency is to relax the aileron through the inverted. SP is expected to hold the aileron pressure constant through the roll.

error_modes.label: Cloverleaf - the rolling pull to the 90-degree reference on each leaf started early or late, the leaves uneven

texts.0: SP, due to the rolling pull being started well before the vertical on the first leaf and well after it on the second, flew leaves of different shapes with the reference picked up late on each. The rolling pull finished more than 20 degrees short of the 90-degree reference on one leaf and more than 20 degrees past it on the next, with the result that the maneuver had no recognizable shape and was stopped after two leaves. The IP took the controls and flew the recovery.
texts.1: SP, due to the point for the rolling pull being judged differently on each leaf, started the roll early on some leaves and late on others and finished 20 degrees off the 90-degree reference on the worst leaf, at the limit of the tolerance, with the result that the leaves were uneven and the completion heading was reached with a correction. SP started the roll at the same point on the later leaves only after the IP called it. The maneuver was completed within the limitations.
texts.2: SP, due to the rolling pull being started a beat early on the first leaf and a beat late on the second, flew leaves that differed slightly in shape and finished about 15 degrees off the 90-degree reference on the worst leaf, between the desired and the maximum tolerance, with the result that a small correction was needed on the completion heading. SP recognized the difference against the reference, started the roll at the same point on the later leaves and completed the maneuver without prompting. The leaves became even by the fourth.
texts.3: SP started the rolling pull at the same point on each leaf, as the nose approached the vertical, and finished within 10 degrees of the 90-degree reference on every leaf, the four leaves the same shape. No prompting was required.
texts.4: SP flew the cloverleaf with the rolling pull started at exactly the same point on each leaf, the roll finishing on the 90-degree reference within a degree or two and the four leaves identical in shape. Nothing in the cloverleaf needed a correction.
texts.marginal: SP kept the cloverleaf inside the required standard, but the rolling pull was started at a slightly different point on each leaf on most maneuvers and the finish sat near the 10 degree edge of the band off the reference on the worst leaf. The tendency is to judge the roll point afresh on every leaf. SP is expected to start the rolling pull at the same point on every leaf.
